[[File:480.jpg|thumb|The posse tasked with the [[The Assault on Fort Mercer|assault]] on [[Fort Mercer]] contains most of the major and supporting characters in the [[New Austin]] [[Missions in Redemption#New Austin Chapter|chapter]].|300x300px]]
'''[[Characters]]''' are the driving force behind the narrative of ''[[Red Dead Redemption]]'', and include the various personalities and figures the player may and will encounter throughout their time in the game.

This page lists characters encountered during ''Redemption's'' single-player gameplay only, please see [[Multiplayer Characters]] for details on characters available in [[Redemption Multiplayer|multiplayer-mode]] gameplay.

==Protagonists==
{|class="wikitable" style="background-color:#222222;"
!<imagemap>
File:JohnMarston-RDR1.jpg|center|200px
default [[John Marston]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[John Marston]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''John Marston''' is the primary protagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. Previously a member of the dangerous [[Dutch's Gang|Van der Linde gang]], John left the outlaw lifestyle to raise his family after a [[Our Best Selves|botched train robbery]]. He is forced by agents representing the [[Bureau of Investigation]] to hunt down his former brothers-in-arms across the dying Wild West.<br><br>John is a hardened and serious man trying to leave behind his bloody past as a dangerous outlaw, despite still being labeled as such by his former associates and government sources.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Jack Marston 1911.png|center|200px
default [[Jack Marston]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Jack Marston]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Outlaw's Return|"The Outlaw's Return"]]<br><br>'''Jack Marston''' is the only surviving child of John, and the secondary protagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. He was born while his parents were still members of the Van der Linde gang and as a result was also raised by the gang's members. He is kidnapped alongside his mother [[Abigail Marston|Abigail]] by government agents to serve as leverage against John.<br><br>Jack is a bright and curious young man, preferring to read books about adventures and heroes over shooting, although he is eager to impress his father with his growing skills; however, the loss of his family and the other members of the gang in his adolescence has largely impacted his life. By young adulthood, he is a different person from the one he was as a child. He deals with personality issues because of this.
|}

==Central characters==
{|class="wikitable" style="background-color:#222222;"
!<imagemap>
File:Edgar Ross Bureau PS5.jpeg|center|200px
default [[Edgar Ross]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Edgar Ross]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''Edgar Ross''' is the main antagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. He is the appointed chief of an American federal outfit called the Bureau of Investigation, tasked with civilizing the dying Old West, and in the process take down infamous members of the now-defunct Van der Linde gang. He kidnaps John's family and forces him into hunting down his former associates, one by one.<br><br>Ross is a man of modernism with preferences for [[High Power Pistol|semi-automatic weapons]] and [[Automobile|automobiles]]. He is sarcastic and calm, but also ruthless and sadistic enough to further his career and bring his own view of justice by any means.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Billw1911.png|center|200px
default [[Bill Williamson]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Bill Williamson]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''Bill Williamson''' is the tertiary antagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. He is the dangerous leader of the [[New Austin]]-based [[Williamson Gang]] and a former member of the Van der Linde gang. He is the first of the three former associates John is forced to hunt down, with the two originally being close friends who grew apart due to Bill's jealousy towards John. Now basing himself at [[Fort Mercer]], Bill terrorizes the entire region.<br><br>He is a cruel and confident outlaw with no qualms about committing the most heinous of crimes, but is also a coward at heart.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:JavierEscuella-Redemption.png|center|200px
default [[Javier Escuella]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Javier Escuella]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Gates of El Presidio|"The Gates of El Presidio"]]<br><br>'''Javier Escuella''' is the quaternary antagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. He is the second of three men John is tasked with bringing down. An outlaw of Mexican heritage, Escuella left for [[Nuevo Paraíso]] after the disbandment of the Van der Linde gang; there he became a mercenary and hitman, often working for the [[Mexican Army]].<br><br>Similar to Bill, Escuella is a cowardly man who prefers to avoid John, but at the same time he can also be a quite cunning.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Dutch 1911 PS5.jpeg|center|200px
default [[Dutch van der Linde]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Dutch van der Linde]]
|'''First appearance''': [[At Home with Dutch|"At Home with Dutch"]]<br><br>'''Dutch van der Linde''' is the secondary antagonist of ''Red Dead Redemption''. He is the final man John is tasked with hunting down, and the leader of both the original Van der Linde gang and the principally [[Native Americans|Native American]][[Dutch's Gang]], as well as John, Bill and Javier's former mentor figure. He is the most notorious criminal in [[West Elizabeth]] and the biggest enemy of the Bureau and its attempt to civilize the region.<br><br>Dutch is a charismatic yet violent and dangerous man who is ready to wage his war against technology and governmental expansion by any means necessary.
|}


==Major characters==
{|class="wikitable" style="background-color:#222222;"
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr bonnie macfarlane square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Bonnie MacFarlane]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Bonnie MacFarlane]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''Bonnie MacFarlane''' is a rancher based in New Austin and the first major ally John gains in ''Red Dead Redemption''. She is the operator of [[MacFarlane's Ranch]], a sizable settlement that keeps thriving as the old ways die out. Despite not knowing him at all, she helps John when the latter is injured in an encounter with Williamson, and she proceeds to introduce the former outlaw to the ways and manners of the region.<br><br>Bonnie is a hard-working and independent woman in a male-dominated land, and tries her best to help her [[Drew MacFarlane|father]] in managing her family farm.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr leigh johnson square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Leigh Johnson]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Leigh Johnson]]
|'''First Appearance''': [[Political Realities in Armadillo|"Political Realities in Armadillo"]]<br><br>'''Leigh Johnson''' is the long-serving Marshal of the town of [[Armadillo]] and a member of the [[U.S. Marshals|Marshals Service]]. He is one of the few remaining honest and stern lawmen remaining in the New Austin region, fighting against outlaw outfits such as the [[Walton's Gang]] and [[Bollard Twins Gang]]. Upon John's arrival to the region, Johnson is contacted by the Bureau of Investigation to aid him in the hunt for Bill Williamson.<br><br>The Marshal is rather sarcastic and is never afraid to draw blood in order to protect his area of law enforcement.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Nigel West Dickens PS5.jpg|center|200px
default [[Nigel West Dickens]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Nigel West Dickens]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Old Swindler Blues|"Old Swindler Blues"]]<br><br>'''Nigel West Dickens''', also known as the '''Snake Oil Guy''', is an elderly con-man posing as a revolutionary salesman, travelling across the American countryside. He sells what he calls "[[Nigel West Dickens' Elixir]]", which he claims can cure people of the most horrible diseases while in reality the elixir is nothing but a scheme.<br><br>An unlikely ally to John, West Dickens is a jovial and mild-mannered elder in nice dress. He will always do his best to assist John, sometimes due to the former outlaw's threats.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Seth Briars PS5.jpg|center|200px
default [[Seth Briars]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Seth Briars]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exhuming and Other Fine Hobbies|"Exhuming and Other Fine Hobbies"]]<br><br>'''Seth Briars''' is a deranged treasure hunter who also happens to be both an associate of West Dickens, and a one-time ally to the Williamson Gang. Despite this, all Seth is concerned with is finding his fabled treasure, for which he left his old business and family years ago.<br><br>He is a misanthrope and a crazy man, and works with John solely because both gain something from the cooperation.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr irish square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Irish]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Irish]]
|'''First appearance''': [[A Frenchman, a Welshman and an Irishman|"A Frenchman, a Welshman and an Irishman"]]<br><br>'''Irish''' is an arms dealer and local drinker around the area of [[Thieves' Landing]], and another unlikely associate of West Dickens. He is acquainted with many outlaws, although most of them either dislike or turn on him due to his constant lies, back-stabbing and general unreliability.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr vincente santa (better).jpg|center|170px
default [[Vincente de Santa]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Vincente de Santa]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Civilization, at Any Price|"Civilization, at Any Price"]]<br><br>Captain '''Vincente de Santa''' is a Captain in the [[Mexican Army]] and the right-hand man of Colonel [[Agustin Allende]], the governor of Nuevo Paraíso. De Santa helps his superior in leading a war against [[Abraham Reyes]]' [[Reyes' Rebels|rebels]]. He strikes a partnership with John in which he will deliver Escuela to him in return for John fighting alongside the Mexican forces.<br><br>De Santa is often joked by his peers and enemies and is a rumored homosexual, with tales about his affair with a [[Quique Montemayor|local bartender]] in [[Escalera]].
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr agustin allende.jpg|center|200px
default [[Agustin Allende]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Agustin Allende]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Demon Drink|"The Demon Drink"]]<br><br>Colonel '''Agustin Allende''' is the governor of Nuevo Paraíso and the right-hand man of Mexico's current leader, General [[Ignacio Sanchez]]. Under the General's commands, he leads an oppression against the rebels led by Abraham Reyes, and oversees Marston's work with De Santa.<br><br>Allende is noted as a highly cruel and lustful man, often kidnapping and raping young women. He is also dismissive of his own men, and tends to lash out at De Santa.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:PS5 Landon Ricketts.png|center|200px
default [[Landon Ricketts]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Landon Ricketts]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Gunslinger's Tragedy|"The Gunslinger's Tragedy"]]<br><br>'''Landon Ricketts''' is a famous gunslinger from America who after years of gunfights decided to retire to Mexico, where he lives in [[Chuparosa]] and serves as a part-time defender of the town against both bandits and the Mexican Army. He is also a friend of the Mexican rebels and cares deeply for the rebels' right-hand woman, [[Luisa Fortuna]].<br><br>Ricketts briefly serves as a shooting teacher to John, and the two team up to fight off bandits and soldiers.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr luisa fortuna square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Luisa Fortuna]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Luisa Fortuna]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Landon Ricketts Rides Again|"Landon Ricketts Rides Again"]]<br><br>'''Luisa Fortuna''' is a young teacher living in [[Campo Mirada]], but also one of the rebellion's leaders and is said to be the fiance of the rebel leader Reyes. She becomes a major ally for John after he saves her from Mexican soldiers.<br><br>Despite her youth, Luisa is a fearless rebel without any problem to risk her life, and is fully dedicated for the liberation of Mexico.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Abraham Reyes PS5.jpg|center|200px
default [[Abraham Reyes]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Abraham Reyes]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Must a Savior Die?|"Must a Savior Die?"]]<br><br>'''Abraham Reyes''' is the leader of the Mexican rebels and the most wanted man by the current Mexican government. Originally from a rich family, he joined the Mexican rebellion for less than noble reasons, and seems to care more about fame and power than about the state of his country.<br><br>Reyes is a charismatic and out-spoken man with a friendly demeanor, but has questionable habits and opinions.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr harold macdougal square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Harold MacDougal]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Harold MacDougal]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Bear One Another's Burdens|"Bear One Another's Burdens"]]<br><br>Professor '''Harold MacDougal''' is an academy man from Yale tasked with learning and studying about Native-Americans and the final days of the Old West. In spite of his profession, MacDougal is a very naive, ignorant and small-minded individual with little factual knowledge on the Natives. He is also an associate of the Bureau.<br><br>He can be somewhat impatient, loud and hyperactive, and is known to be addicted to cocaine, which he abuses frequently.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Abigail 1911 PS5.jpeg|center|200px
default [[Abigail Marston]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Abigail Marston]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Outlaw's Return|"The Outlaw's Return"]]<br><br>'''Abigail Marston''' is John's wife and Jack's mother; similar to her husband she is a former member of the Van der Linde gang and used to be one of the gang's prostitutes. Her choosing of John as her significant other is one of the things that deteriorated relations between Marston and his then-brothers in arms. Alongside her son she was kidnapped by the Bureau to force John into hunting their former comrades.<br><br>Although illiterate and perhaps not as intelligent as her husband and son, Abigail is a stubborn and strong-headed woman who deeply loves and care about her family. 
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr uncle square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Uncle]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Uncle]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Outlaw's Return|"The Outlaw's Return"]]<br><br>'''Uncle''' is a former drinking partner of John's. He used to be a member of the Van der Linde gang back in the day, but left alongside the Marstons. Nowadays he works as a hired muscle for the Marston Ranch at Beecher's Hope, and lives in their house.<br><br>Despite his occupation, Uncle is normally a lazy and drunk man who rarely does his job properly. In spite of this, he is a good and loyal friend to John and his family.
|}

==Supporting characters==
{| class="sortable wikitable" style="background-color:#222222;"
!<imagemap>
File:ArcherHD.jpeg|center|200px
default [[Archer Fordham]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Archer Fordham]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''Archer Fordham''' is a junior agent of the Bureau of Investigation, as well as Edgar Ross' right hand man and protegé. He often occupies Ross in their constant overseeing of John's quest, and Fordham tends to come into blows with the former outlaw.<br><br>Unlike Ross, Fordham takes his job seriously and rarely jokes around. However, he is far more hot-headed and honest than his cold and calculating mentor.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr amos.jpg|center|200px
default [[Amos]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Amos]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Exodus in America|"Exodus in America"]]<br><br>'''Amos''' is the head rancher at the MacFarlane's Ranch and a close friend with the family. His work there consists of taking care of newly broken horses and tending to the barn. He is also an avid [[Poker]] player whom Marston can play with.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr drew macfarlane.jpg|center|200px
default [[Drew MacFarlane]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Drew MacFarlane]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Wild Horses, Tamed Passions|"Wild Horses, Tamed Passions"]]<br><br>'''Drew MacFarlane''' is the owner of the MacFarlane Ranch and the father of Bonnie. He is an experienced rancher who powered through plagues, wars, outlaw attacks and drought. He is very suspicious towards strangers, including John, but warms up to him due to his deeds for the MacFarlanes.<br><br>Bonnie refers to him as a bull of a man, but also expresses worry due to his advanced age.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr jonah square.jpg|center|200px
default [[Jonah]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Jonah]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Political Realities in Armadillo|"Political Realities in Armadillo"]]<br><br>'''Jonah''' is one of the two deputies serving under Marshal Johnson, alongside Eli. He accompanies Johnson and Marston in several missions.<br><br>Unlike Eli, Jonah is rude, unkempt, dim-witted and belligerent, sometimes getting into fights with either John or his partner Eli, but is unquestionably obedient to his superior.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Eli.jpg|center|200px
default [[Eli]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Eli]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Justice in Pike's Basin|"Justice in Pike's Basin"]]<br><br>'''Eli''' is one of the two deputies serving under Marshal Johnson, alongside Jonah. He accompanies Johnson and Marston in several missions.<br><br>Unlike Jonah, Eli is more mild-mannered and respectful towards John. He is physically strong and appears to be more competent than Jonah when it comes to their duties.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr norman deek (better).jpg|center|200px
default [[Norman Deek]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Norman Deek]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Spare the Rod, Spoil the Bandit|"Spare the Rod, Spoil the Bandit"]]<br><br>'''Norman Deek''' is a member of the Williamson gang and Bill's right-hand man. He tends to be by his leader's side and follow his instructions. According to Marshal Johnson, Deek is cruel enough to be a second-in command, but due to his cowardice can never be a leader.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr espinoza.jpg|center|200px
default [[Espinoza]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Espinoza]]
|'''First appearance''': [[The Demon Drink|"The Demon Drink"]]<br><br>Captain '''Espinoza''' is the left-hand man of Colonel Allende, and is considered more competent than his counterpart and rival, De Santa. Unlike either his superior or fellow Captain, Espinoza is a brave and courageous leader, always fighting with his men against the rebels.<br><br>While being just as violent and ruthless as Allende and De Santa, Espinoza truly believes his ways of oppression will bring peace to the region. He forms mutual respect towards Marston.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Rdr victor melendez02.jpg|center|200px
default [[Victor Melendez]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Victor Melendez]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Must a Savior Die?|"Must a Savior Die?"]]<br><br>'''Victor Melendez''' is one of the Mexican rebels' most prominent members, often working directly underneath Luisa and Reyes himself. He appears in many of their missions.
|-
!<imagemap>
File:Nastas RDR Portrait.png|center|200px
default [[Nastas]]
desc none
</imagemap>
|​[[Nastas]]
|'''First appearance''': [[Bear One Another's Burdens|"Bear One Another's Burdens"]]<br><br>'''Nastas''' is a former member of [[Dutch's Gang]], a gang formed by Dutch from Native-American residents of the West Elizabeth region. Displeased with Dutch's violence and usage of his own people, Nastas became an informant of the Bureau. He is deemed a traitor by his people, but is rescued by John and Ross.
|}

== Trivia ==
* [[John Marston|John]] or [[Jack Marston]] can make remarks at/interact with other NPC's such as the random citizens, by the player pressing B/circle/R(keyboard). The remarks vary from insults to compliments, depending on the player's [[Honor]] and [[Fame]].
